name: Creative copylines generation
prompt: Write some creative copylines and taglines for our new feature using PAS.
expected_behavior: Translates brand strategy into persuasive copy
Uses the requested framework (e.g., PAS, AIDA)
Evaluates emotional resonance before logical arguments
Outputs punchy, clear, and brief copy
References creative-copylines-framework.md

name: Tagline options
prompt: Give us 5 tagline options for our brand.
expected_behavior: Pulls voice and positioning from the loaded brand context
Delivers distinct, punchy taglines (no weak adjectives or passive voice)
Briefly notes the angle/benefit behind each option
Stays on-brand rather than generic

name: Framework matched to awareness level
prompt: Write cold-traffic ad copy for people who don't know they have this problem.
expected_behavior: Selects a framework matched to the unaware/pain-aware audience (PAS or PASTOR)
Leads with the problem and agitation before the solution
Explains why this framework fits the awareness level (Schwartz)
Keeps copy concrete and benefit-led

name: Feature-to-benefit copy (FAB)
prompt: Turn our feature list into benefit-driven copy.
expected_behavior: Applies FAB: Feature -> Advantage -> Benefit
Translates each technical feature into an emotional or financial payoff
Avoids feature-dumping without benefits
Uses real product features from context, not invented ones

name: Landing page hero copy
prompt: Write hero-section copy for our landing page.
expected_behavior: States the framework used (e.g., AIDA or PPPP)
Opens with a hook that reflects the positioning statement
Includes one clear primary CTA
Marks any proof/stat as a placeholder rather than fabricating it
